<STRUCT_0001>
We have already seen in the case of morphisms of algebraic spaces,
that it is necessary to allow extensions of the fractions fields
in order to get the correct notion of the valuative criterion.
See Morphisms of Spaces, Example
<REF_0001>.
Still, for morphisms between separated algebraic spaces, such
an extension is not needed
(Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0002>).
However, for morphisms between algebraic stacks, an extension may
be needed even if <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002> are both separated.
For example consider the morphism of algebraic stacks
<MATH_0003>
over the base scheme <MATH_0004>
where <MATH_0005> is a group of order <MATH_0006>. Both source and target are separated
algebraic stacks and the morphism is proper. Whence it
satisfies the uniqueness and existence parts of the valuative criterion
(see Lemma <REF_0003>).
But on the other hand, there is a diagram
<MATH_0007>
where no dotted arrow exists with <MATH_0008> and
<MATH_0009>. Namely, the top horizontal arrow is given
by a <MATH_0010>-torsor over the spectrum of <MATH_0011>. Since any <MATH_0012>-torsor
over the strictly henselian local ring <MATH_0013> is trivial, we see
that if a dotted arrow always exists, then every <MATH_0014>-torsor over
<MATH_0015> is trivial. This is not true because <MATH_0016>
and by Kummer theory <MATH_0017>-torsors over <MATH_0018> are classified by
<MATH_0019> which is nontrivial.
